decision: settings page is a native GPUI page on the strip (strip://settings), not a local HTML page in CEF
why: every state the page shows or edits already lives in Rust (typed Config, keybinds, the file path); HTML needs a new bridge (CEF console/process-message/V8 binding in the 1.4k-line C++ shim, or a localhost socket any web page could hit) plus untyped JS on the far side, and keybinding capture needs raw shell keystrokes that CEF would swallow. Native reuses the key router, palette-style rendering and the shell's scroll, adds no C++ and no IPC, and the state machine unit-tests without a browser. Cost: form widgets are hand-drawn rows (no color picker), acceptable for 8 colors, 8 scalars and a key list
evidence: browser-ui/src/settings_page.rs; unit tests on SettingsPage::on_key; private headless cage run: ctrl+, opens it, keys/click/wheel edit and scroll it

decision: settings write-back = one generated STRIP_SETTINGS block at the top of browser.lua, merged over the returned table by the loader; nothing else in the file is rewritten
why: the file is user Lua with comments, locals, hooks and commands, so regenerating it (or round-tripping through a Lua AST) would destroy code. A block can be replaced by marker lines with no parsing of user code. It sits at the TOP because a Lua chunk cannot have statements after its final `return`; it assigns a global that Config::parse reads after running the file and merges per key (theme/behavior) or as a whole list (keys, same all-or-nothing meaning as a plain keys table) BEFORE typed parsing so clamps still apply. Rejected: appended block (invalid after `return`), block inside a comment that the loader parses (live-looking code that is inert reads as disabled), sidecar file or JSON (second store, forbidden), in-place value edits (needs a Lua parser, fragile with functions)
evidence: browser-config/src/settings.rs; tests edit_round_trips_through_the_real_loader_and_keeps_user_code (bytes outside the block identical, Config::load gives the edited values, commands and hooks survive) and reset_removes_the_override_and_then_the_block

decision: edit = validate, parse the candidate with the real loader, check the block round-trips, then temp file + fsync + rename in the target's directory; a refused write leaves the file untouched
why: the existing watcher already reloads on change and keeps the old config on a parse error, so no apply path is added; validating first means the GUI cannot be what breaks the file, and Config::parse silently ignores wrong-typed values (a string for gap just defaults) so kind checks live on the GUI side. A symlinked browser.lua (dotfiles) is resolved with canonicalize so the rename does not replace the link, and watch_config now also watches the target directory, otherwise an edit of a symlinked config never hot-reloaded
evidence: tests invalid_values_are_refused_and_file_is_untouched, broken_user_file_is_not_written, unterminated_block_is_refused, symlinked_config_is_edited_in_place; headless run: gap 12 to 30 applied (config.get), no .tmp left, a hand-broken file keeps the old config and settings.get load_error names it

decision: editable fields are derived from the serde shape of Theme and Behavior (settings::fields), kind inferred from the value type; keys have their own editor; commands/events (Lua code) show as counts only
why: a hand-kept field table would drift from the typed Config; deriving means a new field appears in the page and in settings.get with one change. A test destructures Config exhaustively so a new top-level field forces a decision, and another asserts every Theme/Behavior value has an editor kind. serde_json preserve_order keeps declaration order. Numbers are normalized at f32 precision so 0.18 + 0.01 writes 0.19, not 0.19000000000000003
evidence: tests every_config_value_is_an_editable_field, every_default_value_passes_its_own_validation, nudged_floats_round_trip

decision: settings.open is a Request (palette, prompt, keybind, agent), default ctrl+, in default_keys and the shipped browser.lua; settings.get and settings.set join the agent API; an existing browser.lua with its own keys table does not gain ctrl+, automatically
why: a keys table replacing every default is documented behavior, so injecting a default into user key lists would break it; the shipped file and docs say to add the line, and the palette, prompt and agent API work regardless. settings.set exists so agents and the headless check use the exact write path the GUI uses; keybinding edits stay in the page (a second key-editing API would be YAGNI)
